chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Bromoethane (CH3CH2Br) is treated with 1H NMR spectrometer?

options.label: A
options.text: Triplet (3H) at δ 1.7 ppm and Quartet (2H) at δ 3.4 ppm

options.label: C
options.text: Doublet of doublets with large coupling constant J = 16 Hz

options.label: D
options.text: 1 positive signal (CH3) and 3 negative signals (CH2 groups)

questions.correct_answer: Triplet (3H) at δ 1.7 ppm and Quartet (2H) at δ 3.4 ppm
questions.explanation: Treating Bromoethane (CH3CH2Br) with 1H NMR spectrometer yields Triplet (3H) at δ 1.7 ppm and Quartet (2H) at δ 3.4 ppm. Rationale: Vicinal coupling between methyl (3H) and methylene (2H) generates reciprocal quartet-triplet patterns.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 2-Bromopropane ((CH3)2CHBr) into Doublet (6H) at δ 1.7 ppm and Septet (1H) at δ 4.3 ppm?
questions.explanation: To convert 2-Bromopropane ((CH3)2CHBr) into Doublet (6H) at δ 1.7 ppm and Septet (1H) at δ 4.3 ppm, the appropriate reagent is 1H NMR spectrometer. Rationale: The methine proton splits the 6 equivalent methyl protons into a doublet; methyls split methine into a septet.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: What is the expected major product when tert-Butyl methyl ether is treated with 1H NMR spectrometer?

options.label: A
options.text: Doublet of doublets with large coupling constant J = 16 Hz

options.label: B
options.text: Two singlets: δ 1.2 ppm (9H) and δ 3.2 ppm (3H)

questions.correct_answer: Two singlets: δ 1.2 ppm (9H) and δ 3.2 ppm (3H)
questions.explanation: Treating tert-Butyl methyl ether with 1H NMR spectrometer yields Two singlets: δ 1.2 ppm (9H) and δ 3.2 ppm (3H). Rationale: Both the 9 tert-butyl protons and 3 methoxy protons have no adjacent hydrogens, appearing as clean singlets.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 1,4-Dimethylbenzene (p-xylene) into Singlet (6H, methyls) and Singlet (4H, aromatic)?
questions.explanation: To convert 1,4-Dimethylbenzene (p-xylene) into Singlet (6H, methyls) and Singlet (4H, aromatic), the appropriate reagent is 1H NMR spectrometer. Rationale: Molecular symmetry makes all 4 aromatic ring hydrogens equivalent, producing a single 4H singlet at δ 7.0 ppm.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.topic: 13C NMR signal count in symmetric ketone
questions.question: What is the expected major product when 3-Pentanone ((CH3CH2)2C=O) is treated with 13C NMR spectrometer?

options.label: B
options.text: Sharp singlet downfield at δ 9.8-10.0 ppm

questions.explanation: Treating 3-Pentanone ((CH3CH2)2C=O) with 13C NMR spectrometer yields 3 distinct carbon signals. Rationale: Due to plane of symmetry, the molecule contains 3 types of carbon: methyl (C1/C5), methylene (C2/C4), and carbonyl (C3).

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 1-Butanol (CH3CH2CH2CH2OH) into 1 positive signal (CH3) and 3 negative signals (CH2 groups)?
questions.explanation: To convert 1-Butanol (CH3CH2CH2CH2OH) into 1 positive signal (CH3) and 3 negative signals (CH2 groups), the appropriate reagent is DEPT-135 13C NMR spectrometer. Rationale: DEPT-135 displays CH3 and CH carbons pointing upward (positive) and CH2 carbons pointing downward (negative).

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: Which starting material will react with 1H NMR spectrometer to yield Doublet of doublets with large coupling constant J = 16 Hz as the major product?
questions.explanation: trans-Cinnamic acid (trans-PhCH=CHCOOH) reacts with 1H NMR spectrometer to yield Doublet of doublets with large coupling constant J = 16 Hz. Rationale: Trans-alkene protons exhibit large coupling constants (J = 14-18 Hz), whereas cis-alkenes show J = 6-12 Hz.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO) is treated with 1H NMR spectrometer?

options.label: A
options.text: Doublet (6H) at δ 1.7 ppm and Septet (1H) at δ 4.3 ppm

options.label: C
options.text: Sharp singlet downfield at δ 9.8-10.0 ppm

questions.correct_answer: Sharp singlet downfield at δ 9.8-10.0 ppm
questions.explanation: Treating Benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO) with 1H NMR spectrometer yields Sharp singlet downfield at δ 9.8-10.0 ppm. Rationale: Strong magnetic anisotropy and inductive deshielding from the carbonyl group shift the formyl proton to δ 10 ppm.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: Which starting material will react with 1H NMR spectrometer to yield Broad singlet downfield at δ 11.5-12.0 ppm as the major product?
questions.explanation: Acetic acid (CH3COOH) reacts with 1H NMR spectrometer to yield Broad singlet downfield at δ 11.5-12.0 ppm. Rationale: Extensive hydrogen bonding and electron withdrawal strongly deshield the carboxyl proton beyond δ 11 ppm.

questions.chapter_title: Structure Determination: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Acetone ((CH3)2C=O) is treated with 13C NMR spectrometer?

options.label: A
options.text: Triplet (3H) at δ 1.7 ppm and Quartet (2H) at δ 3.4 ppm

options.label: C
options.text: 1 positive signal (CH3) and 3 negative signals (CH2 groups)

options.label: D
options.text: Doublet of doublets with large coupling constant J = 16 Hz

questions.explanation: Treating Acetone ((CH3)2C=O) with 13C NMR spectrometer yields Downfield signal at δ 206 ppm. Rationale: The highly polarized, sp2-hybridized carbonyl carbon resonates far downfield between δ 190 and 220 ppm.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with 1H NMR spectrometer to yield Two singlets: δ 1.2 ppm (9H) and δ 3.2 ppm (3H) as the major product?
questions.explanation: tert-Butyl methyl ether reacts with 1H NMR spectrometer to yield Two singlets: δ 1.2 ppm (9H) and δ 3.2 ppm (3H). Rationale: Both the 9 tert-butyl protons and 3 methoxy protons have no adjacent hydrogens, appearing as clean singlets.

questions.explanation: To convert 3-Pentanone ((CH3CH2)2C=O) into 3 distinct carbon signals, the appropriate reagent is 13C NMR spectrometer. Rationale: Due to plane of symmetry, the molecule contains 3 types of carbon: methyl (C1/C5), methylene (C2/C4), and carbonyl (C3).

questions.explanation: To convert trans-Cinnamic acid (trans-PhCH=CHCOOH) into Doublet of doublets with large coupling constant J = 16 Hz, the appropriate reagent is 1H NMR spectrometer. Rationale: Trans-alkene protons exhibit large coupling constants (J = 14-18 Hz), whereas cis-alkenes show J = 6-12 Hz.
